title: Medtronic MiniMed predictive low-glucose suspend reducing hypoglycemia with a successful pregnancy
summary: MiniMed 640G predictive low-glucose suspend cut hypoglycemia in a T1D woman after two miscarriages; term birth of a 4,137 g boy.
account: In a case report published in Diabetology International on 6 March 2021 (dates of events not stated; publication date used), a 22-year-old Brazilian woman living in Japan with type 1 diabetes for 11 years, who had miscarried at 7 and 9 weeks in two earlier pregnancies, was switched at about 6 weeks of her third pregnancy to a Medtronic MiniMed 640G sensor-augmented pump with predictive low glucose suspend. The pump suspended insulin for about 249 minutes per day; hypoglycemic episodes fell from 2.1–2.5 to 1.4 per day and time below 70 mg/dL from 1.1–1.4% to 0.5%. She delivered a 4,137 g boy by cesarean section at 39 weeks and 3 days with no significant complications.
purpose: Predictive low glucose suspend is built to stop insulin delivery when sensor glucose is predicted to fall low, to avoid hypoglycemia; the benefit was that purpose, with a successful pregnancy as the downstream outcome.
system: Medtronic MiniMed sensor-augmented pump / automated insulin delivery with predictive low glucose suspend (SmartGuard)

ratings.reason: After two miscarriages, hypoglycemia frequency and glucose variability fell on the device and the pregnancy reached term with a healthy infant; a life-changing benefit, though the source does not prove the device caused the live birth.

ai_role.statement: The pump's predictive algorithm autonomously suspended insulin for about four hours a day, which the authors link to fewer hypoglycemic episodes and lower variability; obstetric and diabetes care were delivered by clinicians, and the causal link to carrying the pregnancy is inferred, not demonstrated.

produced_by: A person with type 1 diabetes and frequent or unrecognised hypoglycemia uses a Medtronic pump with CGM and predictive low glucose suspend enabled
Sensor glucose is predicted to fall and the algorithm suspends basal insulin
Hypoglycemia frequency and variability fall and the clinical goal (pregnancy, restored awareness) is reached
must_hold: Sensor is worn and calibrated with suspend enabled
The user does not override suspensions

echoes.setting: 45-year-old man with type 1 diabetes since 1996 and impaired hypoglycemia awareness, Czechia; MiniMed 780G SmartGuard started mid-2021 after his driving license was suspended in April 2021; no severe hypoglycemia since, Clarke and Gold scores 6 to 2 by early 2022, license reinstated, time below range 23% to 1% by June 2024 (publication date)
echoes.source: Zadáková & Horová (2025). Front Clin Diabetes Healthc 6:1536038. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11886589/

headline: MiniMed 640G cuts hypoglycemia; mother delivers a 4,137 g boy

later.note: No development for this patient after the 2021 case report was found; the 2025 MiniMed 780G report already recorded as an echo concerns a different patient.
